aiTitle: Doctest PHP機能を統合し例文表示を自動化

content: https://github.com/k-kinzal/doctest-php の機能をphp-ai-toolkitに取り込んでください。またPHPStanのカスタムルールとして公開インターフェース、つまり@visiblityでpublicになっているものはExampleを記載することを強制してください。またPHPUnitでの実行、DocGenでのExampleの表示＆単独実行、skillsで別PJへの反映を可能にしてください。この作業はmainブランチで行い、終わったらコミットしてください。もしあなたが権限的に編集できないファイルがあればCodex CLIに依頼してください。

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- external-codex-ai-perspective: Use this agent when you want to get a different perspective or opinion from another AI, switch viewpoints on a problem, or verify your thinking through an external lens. This agent is for read-only, side-effect-free tasks such as research, web searches, reviews, analysis, brainstorming, or validation - NOT for tasks that involve writing files, executing code, or making changes to the system.

<example>
Context: The user is debugging a complex algorithm and wants a fresh perspective on the approach.
user: "I've been stuck on this sorting optimization for hours. Can you get another perspective on whether my approach makes sense?"
assistant: "Let me use the external-ai-perspective agent to get a fresh viewpoint on your sorting optimization approach."
<commentary>
Since the user wants a different perspective on their algorithm approach, use the Task tool to launch the external-ai-perspective agent to consult another AI for alternative viewpoints.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The user wants to validate their architectural decision before implementing.
user: "Before I implement this microservices architecture, I want to make sure I'm not missing any major concerns."
assistant: "I'll use the external-ai-perspective agent to get an independent review of your microservices architecture plan."
<commentary>
Since the user wants validation of their architectural decision, use the external-ai-perspective agent to get an external opinion without making any changes to the codebase.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The user is reviewing code and wants additional opinions on potential issues.
user: "Can you check if there are any security concerns in this authentication flow that I might have overlooked?"
assistant: "Let me consult the external-ai-perspective agent to get another viewpoint on potential security concerns in your authentication flow."
<commentary>
Since this is a review task seeking different perspectives on security, use the external-ai-perspective agent for a read-only analysis.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

attachment.content:
- browser-use: Browser automation via browser-use CLI: navigate websites, fill forms, take screenshots, extract data, interact with web pages, web testing.
- buddy: buddyctl CLI: observe the desktop, start/stop Buddy sessions, run session tools (pointer, keyboard, gestures, attention). For long-running Observe watching, also use buddy-observe.
- clickhouse-ingest: Insert data into ClickHouse data warehouse: HTTP/native INSERT, bulk loading, agent session logs, app events. NOT for schema changes (use clickhouse-ops) or querying (use clickhouse-query).
- clickhouse-ops: ClickHouse data warehouse on GPU server (192.168.10.4): Docker Compose, schema DDL, migrations, user admin, retention/TTL, server config. NOT for writing data (use clickhouse-ingest) or querying (use clickhouse-query).
- clickhouse-query: Query and analyze ClickHouse data warehouse: SELECT patterns, agent session analysis, app event analytics, materialized views, system introspection. NOT for schema changes (use clickhouse-ops) or data insertion (use clickhouse-ingest).
- comfyui: ComfyUI on GPU server (192.168.10.4): image generation, inpainting, LoRA, checkpoints, custom nodes, workflow execution, diffusion workflows, data generation pipelines.
- find-docs: Fetch up-to-date technical docs, API references, and code examples for libraries, frameworks, SDKs, CLI tools, and cloud services. Prefer when documentation accuracy matters or model knowledge may be outdated.
- gal-advice: Use when the agent wants advice or a blunt second opinion. Run the gal command to get an outside perspective on the situation.
- gpu-containers: Docker containers on GPU server (192.168.10.4): NVIDIA GPU workloads, Docker Compose, container management, service orchestration, image builds, CUDA deployment.
- iter: iter CLI: run, compose up, ps, logs, stop, kill, rm, inspect, validate. Foreground/detached runners, ULID/name resolution. Entry point before authoring Iterfile or compose.iter.
- iter-compose: Author or modify compose.iter — iter's multi-service orchestration. Streams, services (build/inline), triggers (cron/watch/files/command/webhook). Stream binding, process model, standalone trigger binaries.
- iter-iterfile: Author or modify an Iterfile (single-service HCL config for iter run). Blocks: workspace, agent, runner, prompt, stream, on-event. Workspace kinds, agent CLI kinds, wait/loop behaviors, conditional expressions.
- ollama: Ollama on GPU server (192.168.10.4): LLM inference, chat, vision (LLaVA), embeddings, structured JSON output, tool calling, model management, SD prompt writing via LLM.
- openwork: Work marketplace where Humans and AI Agents hire each other. Find jobs, place bids, deliver work, get paid.
- otel-collector-ops: Operate/configure OTel Collector and LGTM deployments: receivers, processors, exporters, pipelines, health checks, signal routing. Debug dropped telemetry after it leaves the app. NOT for app SDK code or querying.
- otel-instrumentation: Add/fix OpenTelemetry instrumentation in application code: OTLP exporters, context propagation, resource attributes, spans, metrics, logs. Debug missing telemetry before it reaches the Collector. NOT for Collector config or querying.
- otel-observe-api: Observe/query existing telemetry via Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo APIs. PromQL, LogQL, trace search/fetch, stack health, datasources. NOT for adding instrumentation (use otel-instrumentation) or Collector config (use otel-collector-ops).
- setup-toolkit-agents-md: Set up AGENTS.md with project conventions and AI agent guidelines for a PHP project. Use when asked to create AGENTS.md, set up AI agent guidelines, or configure project conventions for AI agents.
- setup-toolkit-deptrac: Set up Deptrac architecture dependency analysis for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure Deptrac, enforce architecture boundaries, validate layer dependencies, create deptrac.yaml, add architecture checks to Composer scripts or CI, or adapt architecture rules for PHP web apps, CLI apps, workers, packages, libraries, modular monoliths, or reusable components.
- setup-toolkit-doc-gen: Set up DocGen static documentation generation for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure doc-gen, doc.yaml, API documentation generation, a docs.rs-style documentation site, GitHub Pages documentation hosting, multi-package or monorepo documentation, documenting vendor packages, architecture layer visualization from deptrac, per-method test coverage references in documentation, executable doctest examples in docs, documentation that compares two git revisions, incremental documentation builds with a parse and page cache, per-pull-request documentation previews, or Composer scripts and CI jobs that publish generated PHP documentation.
- setup-toolkit-github-actions: Set up GitHub Actions CI for php-ai-toolkit PHP projects. Use when asked to create or update .github/workflows/ci.yml, run toolkit checks in CI, pin GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs, align CI with supported PHP versions, or harden workflow permissions and concurrency for Composer, PHPUnit, ParaTest, PHPStan, PHP-CS-Fixer, PHPCompatibility, LocGuard, TreeGuard, ScopeGuard, and Deptrac.
- setup-toolkit-infection: Set up Infection mutation testing for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure Infection, infection.json5, mutation testing, mutation score (MSI) or covered MSI thresholds, a mutation score gate that differs between the default branch and pull requests, mutation testing of changed lines only, Composer scripts for Infection, CI jobs for mutation testing, or when asked why a test suite with high coverage still lets mutants escape.
- setup-toolkit-loc-guard: Set up LocGuard source metrics checks for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure loc-guard, loc.yaml, source line-count limits, NCLOC limits, class/trait/interface/enum length limits, function or method length limits, cyclomatic complexity limits, LocGuard reporters, AI-oriented metrics reports, Composer scripts for LocGuard, or CI checks for PHP source metrics without PHPMD.
- setup-toolkit-php-compatibility: Set up PHPCompatibility cross-version checks for a PHP project. Use when asked to verify code matches the supported PHP version, detect syntax or functions newer than the minimum PHP, enforce a PHP version floor, stop 8.1+ syntax (readonly, enums, first-class callables, new-in-initializer) in an 8.0 project, configure PHPCompatibility or PHP_CodeSniffer for compatibility, create phpcs.xml.dist, or add a compatibility gate to Composer scripts or CI.
- setup-toolkit-php-cs-fixer: Set up PHP-CS-Fixer with strict coding standards for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure code formatting, coding standards, or PHP-CS-Fixer.
- setup-toolkit-phpstan: Set up PHPStan with strict configuration and AI error formatter for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure PHPStan, set up static analysis, or enable the AI error formatter.
- setup-toolkit-phpunit: Set up PHPUnit with strict configuration and AI test reporter for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure PHPUnit, set up testing, or enable the AI test reporter.
- setup-toolkit-scope-guard: Set up ScopeGuard namespace visibility checks for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure scope-guard, scope.yaml, the @visibility tag, package private or internal classes, pub(crate) or pub(super) style visibility in PHP, restricting a class to its own namespace, stopping other namespaces from reaching into a package's internals, exempting tests from visibility rules, ScopeGuard reporters, Composer scripts for ScopeGuard, or CI checks for PHP namespace visibility.
- setup-toolkit-tree-guard: Set up TreeGuard directory and file structure checks for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure tree-guard, tree.yaml, directory file-count limits, subdirectory-count limits, nesting depth limits, file or directory naming conventions, allowed or denied file patterns, required files per directory, empty directory detection, TreeGuard reporters, Composer scripts for TreeGuard, or CI checks for PHP project structure.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
# doctest-php

PHPUnit extension for testing examples in PHP docblocks.

Like Python's doctest or Rust's doc tests, doctest-php automatically extracts and runs code examples from your documentation.

## Installation

```bash
composer require --dev doctest/doctest-php
```

## Quick Start

Add the following to your `phpunit.xml`:

```xml
<phpunit>
    <testsuites>
        <!-- Your existing test suites -->
        <testsuite name="Unit">
            <directory>tests</directory>
        </testsuite>

        <!-- Add doctest suite -->
        <testsuite name="Doctest">
            <file>vendor/doctest/doctest-php/DoctestSuite.php</file>
        </testsuite>
    </testsuites>

    <!-- Configure the extension -->
    <extensions>
        <bootstrap class="Doctest\DoctestExtension">
            <parameter name="directories" value="src"/>
        </bootstrap>
    </extensions>
</phpunit>
```

Write examples in your docblocks:

```php
<?php

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 *
 * ```php
 * add(1, 2) // => 3
 * add(-1, 1) // => 0
 * ```
 */
function add(int $a, int $b): int
{
    return $a + $b;
}
```

Run PHPUnit:

```bash
./vendor/bin/phpunit
```

That's it! No test files to create - doctests are automatically discovered and executed.

## Supported Assertion Formats

### Return Value Assertion (`// => expected`)

```php
/**
 * @example
 * add(1, 2) // => 3
 * subtract(5, 3) // => 2
 */
```

### Output Assertion (`// Output: expected`)

```php
/**
 * @example
 * echo greet("World"); // Output: Hello, World!
 */
```

### Exception Assertion (`// throws ExceptionClass`)

```php
/**
 * @example
 * divide(10, 0) // throws DivisionByZeroError
 *
 * @example With message check
 * divide(10, 0) // throws DivisionByZeroError: Cannot divide by zero
 */
```

### Smoke Test (No Assertion)

Code without assertions is treated as a smoke test - it passes if no exception is thrown:

```php
/**
 * @example
 * $repo = new UserRepository();
 * $name = $repo->findNameById(10);
 * echo $name;
 */
```

## Example Formats

### @example Tag

```php
/**
 * @example Basic usage
 * $calc = new Calculator();
 * $calc->add(1, 2) // => 3
 *
 * @example With negative numbers
 * $calc = new Calculator();
 * $calc->add(-5, 3) // => -2
 */
```

### Code Fence (```php)

````php
/**
 * Calculate the sum.
 *
 * ```php
 * $calc = new Calculator();
 * $calc->add(5, 3) // => 8
 * ```
 */
````

## Multi-line Examples with State

Variables persist within a single example block:

```php
/**
 * @example
 * $stack = new Stack();
 * $stack->push(1);
 * $stack->push(2);
 * $stack->pop() // => 2
 * $stack->pop() // => 1
 */
```

## Configuration Options

Configure via extension parameters in `phpunit.xml`:

```xml
<extensions>
    <bootstrap class="Doctest\DoctestExtension">
        <parameter name="directories" value="src,lib"/>
        <parameter name="files" value="functions.php,helpers.php"/>
        <parameter name="exclude" value="**/vendor/**,**/tests/**"/>
        <parameter name="bootstrap" value="tests/bootstrap.php"/>
    </bootstrap>
</extensions>
```

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `directories` | Comma-separated list of directories to scan |
| `files` | Comma-separated list of specific files to scan |
| `exclude` | Comma-separated glob patterns to exclude |
| `bootstrap` | Bootstrap file to load before running doctests |

## Requirements

- PHP 8.1+
- PHPUnit 10.0+ or 11.0+

## License

MIT

 * echo greet("World"); // Output: Hello, World!
 */
```

### Exception Assertion (`// throws ExceptionClass`)

```php
/**
 * @example
 * divide(10, 0) // throws DivisionByZeroError
 *
 * @example With message check
 * divide(10, 0) // throws DivisionByZeroError: Cannot divide by zero
 */
```

### Smoke Test (No Assertion)

Code without assertions is treated as a smoke test - it passes if no exception is thrown:

```php
/**
 * @example
 * $repo = new UserRepository();
 * $name = $repo->findNameById(10);
 * echo $name;
 */
```

## Example Formats

### @example Tag

```php
/**
 * @example Basic usage
 * $calc = new Calculator();
 * $calc->add(1, 2) // => 3

 * @example With negative numbers

 * $calc->add(-5, 3) // => -2
 */

### Code Fence (```php)

````php
/**
 * Calculate the sum.
 *
 * ```php
 * $calc = new Calculator();
 * $calc->add(5, 3) // => 8

 */
````

## Multi-line Examples with State

Variables persist within a single example block:

```php
/**
 * @example
 * $stack = new Stack();
 * $stack->push(1);
 * $stack->push(2);
 * $stack->pop() // => 2
 * $stack->pop() // => 1

## Configuration Options

Configure via extension parameters in `phpunit.xml`:

```xml
<extensions>
    <bootstrap class="Doctest\DoctestExtension">
        <parameter name="directories" value="src,lib"/>
        <parameter name="files" value="functions.php,helpers.php"/>
        <parameter name="exclude" value="**/vendor/**,**/tests/**"/>
        <parameter name="bootstrap" value="tests/bootstrap.php"/>

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `directories` | Comma-separated list of directories to scan |
| `files` | Comma-separated list of specific files to scan |
| `exclude` | Comma-separated glob patterns to exclude |
| `bootstrap` | Bootstrap file to load before running doctests |

- PHP 8.1+
- PHPUnit 10.0+ or 11.0+

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Doctest\Parser;

use Doctest\Scanner\Target;

/**
 * Extracts Example objects from Target docblocks.
 *
 * Supports both at-example tags followed by indented code,
 * and triple-backtick php code fences in markdown style.
 *
 * @example Creating an extractor
 *     $extractor = new \Doctest\Parser\ExampleExtractor();
 *     $extractor instanceof \Doctest\Parser\ExampleExtractor // => true
 */
final class ExampleExtractor
{
    /**
     * Extracts all examples from a target's docblock.
     *
     * @param Target $target The target containing the docblock
     * @return iterable<Example> Examples found in the docblock
     */
    public function extract(Target $target): iterable
    {
        $docblock = $this->cleanDocblock($target->docblock);
        $index = 0;

        // Strategy 1: Extract @example blocks
        yield from $this->extractExampleTags($docblock, $target, $index);

        // Strategy 2: Extract ```php code fences
        yield from $this->extractCodeFences($docblock, $target, $index);
    }

    private function cleanDocblock(string $docblock): string
    {
        // Remove /** and */
        $docblock = preg_replace('/^\/\*\*\s*|\s*\*\/$/s', '', $docblock) ?? $docblock;

        // Remove leading * from each line
        $lines = explode("\n", $docblock);
        $cleaned = [];

        foreach ($lines as $line) {
            // Remove leading whitespace and asterisk
            $cleaned[] = preg_replace('/^\s*\*\s?/', '', $line) ?? $line;
        }

        return implode("\n", $cleaned);
    }

    /**
     * @return iterable<Example>
     */
    private function extractExampleTags(string $docblock, Target $target, int &$index): iterable
    {
        // Split docblock by @example tags
        $parts = preg_split('/(?=@example\b)/', $docblock, -1, PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY);
        if ($parts === false) {
            return;
        }

        foreach ($parts as $part) {
            if (!str_starts_with(trim($part), '@example')) {
                continue;
            }

            $lines = explode("\n", $part);
            $firstLine = array_shift($lines);
            assert($firstLine !== null); // explode always returns at least one element

            // Extract optional description from @example line
            $description = null;
            if (preg_match('/@example\s+(.+)$/', $firstLine, $descMatch)) {
                $description = trim($descMatch[1]);
            }

            // Collect code lines until next @tag or end
            $codeLines = [];
            foreach ($lines as $line) {
                $trimmedLine = trim($line);
                // Stop at next @tag
                if (preg_match('/^@\w+/', $trimmedLine)) {
                    break;
                }
                // Skip empty lines at the beginning
                if ($codeLines === [] && $trimmedLine === '') {
                    continue;
                }
                $codeLines[] = $line;
            }

            // Trim trailing empty lines
            while ($codeLines !== [] && trim(end($codeLines)) === '') {
                array_pop($codeLines);
            }

            $code = implode("\n", $codeLines);
            $code = trim($code);

            if ($code === '') {
                continue;
            }

            // Calculate line number based on offset
            $offset = strpos($docblock, $part);
            $lineNumber = $this->calculateLineNumber($docblock, $offset !== false ? $offset : 0, $target->line);

            yield new Example(
                code: $code,
                target: $target,
                lineNumber: $lineNumber,
                index: $index++,
                description: $description !== '' ? $description : null,
            );
        }
    }

    /**
     * @return iterable<Example>
     */
    private function extractCodeFences(string $docblock, Target $target, int &$index): iterable
    {
        // Match ```php ... ``` blocks
        $pattern = '/```php\s*\n(.*?)```/s';

        if (preg_match_all($pattern, $docblock, $matches, PREG_SET_ORDER | PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE)) {
            foreach ($matches as $match) {
                /** @var array{0: array{0: string, 1: int}, 1: array{0: string, 1: int}} $match */
                $code = trim($match[1][0]);

                if ($code === '') {
                    continue;
                }

                $lineNumber = $this->calculateLineNumber($docblock, $match[0][1], $target->line);

                yield new Example(
                    code: $code,
                    target: $target,
                    lineNumber: $lineNumber,
                    index: $index++,
                );
            }
        }
    }

    private function calculateLineNumber(string $docblock, int $offset, int $baseLine): int
    {
        $beforeMatch = substr($docblock, 0, $offset);
        $linesBeforeMatch = substr_count($beforeMatch, "\n");

        return $baseLine + $linesBeforeMatch + 1;
    }
}

<?php

/**
 * Assertion parsing for doctest-php.
 *
 * @example File-level example: creating parser instance
 *     $parser = new \Doctest\Assertion\AssertionParser();
 *     $parser instanceof \Doctest\Assertion\AssertionParser // => true
 */

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Doctest\Assertion;

use Doctest\Parser\Example;

/**
 * Parses example code to extract statements and assertions.
 *
 * The parser recognizes several assertion formats:
 * - Return value: `expression // => expected_value`
 * - Output: `echo $var; // Output: expected_output`
 * - Exception: `throw new Exception(); // throws Exception`
 * - Exception with message: `throw new Exception("msg"); // throws Exception: msg`
 *
 * Lines without assertions become "smoke test" statements that just verify
 * the code runs without errors.
 */
final class AssertionParser
{
    /**
     * Parse example code and extract assertions.
     *
     * Supported formats:
     * - `expression // => expected_value`
     * - `echo $var; // Output: expected_output`
     * - `throw new Exception(); // throws Exception`
     * - `throw new Exception("msg"); // throws Exception: msg`
     *
     * @param Example $example The example to parse
     * @return ParsedExample The parsed example with statements
     */
    public function parse(Example $example): ParsedExample
    {
        $lines = explode("\n", $example->code);
        $statements = [];
        $currentCode = '';
        $lineNum = 0;

        foreach ($lines as $index => $line) {
            $trimmed = trim($line);

            // Skip empty lines
            if ($trimmed === '') {
                continue;
            }

            $lineNum = $index + 1;

            // Check for return value assertion: code // => expected
            if (preg_match('/^(.+?)\s*\/\/\s*=>\s*(.+)$/', $trimmed, $matches)) {
                $code = $currentCode . trim($matches[1]);
                $currentCode = '';

                $statements[] = new Statement(
                    code: $code,
                    assertion: new Assertion(
                        type: AssertionType::ReturnValue,
                        expectedRaw: trim($matches[2]),
                    ),
                    line: $lineNum,
                );
                continue;
            }

            // Check for output assertion: code // Output: expected
            if (preg_match('/^(.+?)\s*\/\/\s*Output:\s*(.*)$/', $trimmed, $matches)) {
                $code = $currentCode . trim($matches[1]);
                $currentCode = '';

                $statements[] = new Statement(
                    code: $code,
                    assertion: new Assertion(
                        type: AssertionType::Output,
                        expectedRaw: $matches[2],
                    ),
                    line: $lineNum,
                );
                continue;
            }

            // Check for exception assertion: code // throws ExceptionClass: message
            if (preg_match('/^(.+?)\s*\/\/\s*throws\s+(\S+)(?::\s*(.*))?$/', $trimmed, $matches)) {
                $code = $currentCode . trim($matches[1]);
                $currentCode = '';

                $statements[] = new Statement(
                    code: $code,
                    assertion: new Assertion(
                        type: AssertionType::Exception,
                        expectedRaw: $matches[2],
                        exceptionMessage: isset($matches[3]) ? trim($matches[3]) : null,
                    ),
                    line: $lineNum,
                );
                continue;
            }

            // Check if line continues (ends with operators or incomplete syntax)
            if ($this->isIncompleteLine($trimmed)) {
                $currentCode .= $trimmed . ' ';
                continue;
            }

            // Regular statement without assertion (smoke test)
            $code = $currentCode . $trimmed;
            $currentCode = '';

            $statements[] = new Statement(
                code: $code,
                assertion: null,
                line: $lineNum,
            );
        }

        // Handle any remaining code
        if ($currentCode !== '') {
            $statements[] = new Statement(
                code: trim($currentCode),
                assertion: null,
                line: $lineNum,
            );
        }

        return new ParsedExample($example, $statements);
    }

    private function isIncompleteLine(string $line): bool
    {
        // Check for lines that are likely incomplete
        $incompletePatterns = [
            '/\.\s*$/',      // Ends with .
            '/,\s*$/',       // Ends with ,
            '/\(\s*$/',      // Ends with (
            '/\[\s*$/',      // Ends with [
            '/\{\s*$/',      // Ends with {
            '/=>\s*$/',      // Ends with =>
            '/\->\s*$/',     // Ends with ->
            '/::\s*$/',      // Ends with ::
            '/&&\s*$/',      // Ends with &&
            '/\|\|\s*$/',    // Ends with ||
            '/\?\s*$/',      // Ends with ?
        ];

        foreach ($incompletePatterns as $pattern) {
            if (preg_match($pattern, $line)) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }
}

<?php

/**
 * Example execution for doctest-php.
 *
 * @example File-level example: creating executor
 *     $executor = new \Doctest\Executor\ExampleExecutor();
 *     $executor instanceof \Doctest\Executor\ExampleExecutor // => true
 */

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Doctest\Executor;

use Doctest\Assertion\AssertionParser;
use Doctest\Assertion\AssertionResult;
use Doctest\Assertion\AssertionType;
use Doctest\Assertion\ParsedExample;
use Doctest\Assertion\Statement;
use Doctest\Parser\Example;
use LogicException;
use ReflectionClass;
use Throwable;

/**
 * Executes doctest examples and verifies assertions.
 *
 * The executor handles parsing example code, executing statements,
 * and verifying assertions. It supports:
 * - Return value assertions (// =>)
 * - Output assertions (// Output:)
 * - Exception assertions (// throws)
 *
 * @example Creating and checking executor
 *     $executor = new \Doctest\Executor\ExampleExecutor();
 *     $executor instanceof \Doctest\Executor\ExampleExecutor // => true
 */
final class ExampleExecutor
{
    private AssertionParser $parser;

    /** @var list<string> */
    private array $loadedFiles = [];

    /**
     * @param string|null $bootstrap Path to bootstrap file to require before execution
     */
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ?string $bootstrap = null,
    ) {
        $this->parser = new AssertionParser();
    }

    /**
     * Executes an example and returns the result.
     *
     * Parses the example code, executes each statement, and verifies
     * any assertions.
     *
     * @param Example $example The example to execute
     * @return ExecutionResult The execution result
     */
    public function execute(Example $example): ExecutionResult
    {
        $parsed = $this->parser->parse($example);

        return $this->executeParsed($parsed);
    }

    /**
     * Executes a parsed example and returns the result.
     *
     * @param ParsedExample $parsed The parsed example to execute
     * @return ExecutionResult The execution result
     */
    public function executeParsed(ParsedExample $parsed): ExecutionResult
    {
        $context = new ExecutionContext();
        $failures = [];

        // Load bootstrap if configured and not already loaded
        if ($this->bootstrap !== null && !in_array($this->bootstrap, $this->loadedFiles, true)) {
            require_once $this->bootstrap;
            $this->loadedFiles[] = $this->bootstrap;
        }

        // Load the target file to make functions/classes available
        $targetFile = $parsed->example->target->filePath;
        if (!in_array($targetFile, $this->loadedFiles, true)) {
            require_once $targetFile;
            $this->loadedFiles[] = $targetFile;
        }

        foreach ($parsed->statements as $statement) {
            $result = $this->executeStatement($statement, $context);

            if (!$result->passed) {
                $failures[] = $result;
            }
        }

        return new ExecutionResult(
            example: $parsed->example,
            passed: $failures === [],
            failures: $failures,
        );
    }

    private function executeStatement(Statement $statement, ExecutionContext $context): AssertionResult
    {
        // Handle exception assertions specially
        if ($statement->assertion?->type === AssertionType::Exception) {
            return $this->executeWithExpectedException($statement, $context);
        }

        // Regular execution
        try {

<?php

/**
 * Example representation for doctest-php.
 *
 * @example File-level example: example with code
 *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
 *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Function_,
 *         filePath: '/app/helpers.php',
 *         docblock: 'fn docs',
 *         name: 'helper',
 *         line: 1,
 *     );
 *     $example = new \Doctest\Parser\Example('1 + 1', $target, 5, 0);
 *     $example->code // => '1 + 1'
 */

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Doctest\Parser;

use Doctest\Scanner\Target;

/**
 * Represents a single example extracted from a docblock.
 *
 * An Example contains the code to execute, the target it belongs to,
 * and metadata about its location and description.
 *
 * @example Creating an example and getting its name
 *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
 *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Method,
 *         filePath: '/path/to/File.php',
 *         docblock: 'some docs',
 *         name: 'add',
 *         line: 10,
 *         className: 'Calculator',
 *     );
 *     $example = new \Doctest\Parser\Example(
 *         code: '$calc->add(1, 2)',
 *         target: $target,
 *         lineNumber: 15,
 *         index: 0,
 *         description: 'Adding two numbers',
 *     );
 *     $example->getName() // => 'Calculator::add() example #1: Adding two numbers'
 *
 * @example Getting test name
 *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
 *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Class_,
 *         filePath: '/path/to/File.php',
 *         docblock: 'some docs',
 *         name: 'Calculator',
 *         line: 5,
 *     );
 *     $example = new \Doctest\Parser\Example(
 *         code: 'new Calculator()',
 *         target: $target,
 *         lineNumber: 8,
 *         index: 0,
 *     );
 *     $example->getTestName() // => 'Doctest: Calculator example #1 (line 8)'
 */
final class Example
{
    /**
     * @param string $code The example code to execute
     * @param Target $target The target this example belongs to
     * @param int $lineNumber Line number in the source file
     * @param int $index Zero-based index among examples for this target
     * @param string|null $description Optional description from @example tag
     */
    public function __construct(
        public readonly string $code,
        public readonly Target $target,
        public readonly int $lineNumber,
        public readonly int $index,
        public readonly ?string $description = null,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Returns a human-readable name for the example.
     *
     * Combines the target's short name with the example index and optional description.
     */
    public function getName(): string
    {
        $name = $this->target->getShortName();
        $desc = $this->description !== null ? ': ' . $this->description : '';

        return sprintf('%s example #%d%s', $name, $this->index + 1, $desc);
    }

    /**
     * Returns the PHPUnit test name for this example.
     *
     * Includes the example name and line number for identification.
     */
    public function getTestName(): string
    {
        return sprintf(
            'Doctest: %s (line %d)',
            $this->getName(),
            $this->lineNumber,
        );
    }
}

     *

                            type: TargetType::Function_,
                            filePath: $this->filePath,

                            line: $docComment->getStartLine(),

                if ($node instanceof Namespace_) {
                    $this->currentNamespace = null;
                }

                if ($node instanceof Class_) {
                    $this->currentClass = null;
                }

            }
        };

        $traverser = new NodeTraverser();
        $traverser->addVisitor($visitor);
        $traverser->traverse($ast);

<?php

/**
 * Scanner target representation for doctest-php.
 *
 * @example File-level example: creating a class target
 *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
 *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Class_,
 *         filePath: '/app/src/MyClass.php',
 *         docblock: 'class docs',
 *         name: 'MyClass',
 *         line: 10,
 *     );
 *     $target->type // => \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Class_
 */

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Doctest\Scanner;

/**
 * Represents a target (file, class, method, or function) that may contain docblock examples.
 *
 * A Target encapsulates all information needed to identify and process a documented
 * element in the source code, including its type, location, and associated docblock.
 *
 * @example Creating a method target and getting short name
 *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
 *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Method,
 *         filePath: '/path/to/File.php',
 *         docblock: 'some docs',
 *         name: 'myMethod',
 *         line: 10,
 *         namespace: 'App\\Services',
 *         className: 'Calculator',
 *         isStatic: false,
 *     );
 *     $target->getShortName() // => 'Calculator::myMethod()'
 *
 * @example Getting fully qualified name for a class
 *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
 *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Class_,
 *         filePath: '/path/to/File.php',
 *         docblock: 'some docs',
 *         name: 'Calculator',
 *         line: 5,
 *         namespace: 'App\\Services',
 *     );
 *     $target->getFullyQualifiedName() // => 'App\\Services\\Calculator'
 */
final class Target
{
    /**
     * @param TargetType $type The type of this target (file, class, method, or function)
     * @param string $filePath Absolute path to the source file
     * @param string $docblock The raw docblock content including delimiters
     * @param string $name The name of the target (filename, class name, method name, etc.)
     * @param int $line Line number where the docblock starts
     * @param string|null $namespace The namespace of the target, if applicable
     * @param string|null $className The class name, if the target is a method
     * @param bool $isStatic Whether the target is a static method
     */
    public function __construct(
        public readonly TargetType $type,
        public readonly string $filePath,
        public readonly string $docblock,
        public readonly string $name,
        public readonly int $line,
        public readonly ?string $namespace = null,
        public readonly ?string $className = null,
        public readonly bool $isStatic = false,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Returns the fully qualified name of the target.
     *
     * @example Getting FQN for a function
     *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
     *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Function_,
     *         filePath: '/path/to/helpers.php',
     *         docblock: 'some docs',
     *         name: 'calculate',
     *         line: 1,
     *         namespace: 'App\\Helpers',
     *     );
     *     $target->getFullyQualifiedName() // => 'App\\Helpers\\calculate()'
     */
    public function getFullyQualifiedName(): string
    {
        $fqn = $this->namespace !== null ? $this->namespace . '\\' : '';

        return match ($this->type) {
            TargetType::File => $this->filePath,
            TargetType::Class_ => $fqn . $this->name,
            TargetType::Function_ => $fqn . $this->name . '()',
            TargetType::Method => $fqn . $this->className . '::' . $this->name . '()',
        };
    }

    /**
     * Returns the short (unqualified) name of the target.
     *
     * @example Getting short name for a method
     *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
     *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Method,
     *         filePath: '/path/to/File.php',
     *         docblock: 'some docs',
     *         name: 'add',
     *         line: 10,
     *         namespace: 'App\\Services',
     *         className: 'Calculator',
     *     );
     *     $target->getShortName() // => 'Calculator::add()'
     */
    public function getShortName(): string
    {
        return match ($this->type) {
            TargetType::File => basename($this->filePath),
            TargetType::Class_ => $this->name,
            TargetType::Function_ => $this->name . '()',
            TargetType::Method => $this->className . '::' . $this->name . '()',
        };
    }
}

namespace Doctest\TestCase;

use Doctest\Configuration\Configuration;
use Doctest\Executor\ExampleExecutor;
use Doctest\Parser\Example;
use Doctest\Parser\ExampleExtractor;
use Doctest\Scanner\FileScanner;
use Doctest\Scanner\SourceScanner;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Test;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

/**
 * Base class for running doctests as PHPUnit tests.
 *
 * Extend this class and implement the configure() method to run doctests
 * for your project.
 *
 * @example Checking class hierarchy
 *     is_a(\Doctest\TestCase\DoctestRunner::class, \PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase::class, true) // => true
 */
abstract class DoctestRunner extends TestCase
{
    private static ?ExampleExecutor $executor = null;

    /**
     * Override to provide custom configuration.
     *
     * @return Configuration The configuration for doctest scanning
     */
    abstract protected static function configure(): Configuration;

    /**
     * Provides examples as test data.
     *
     * @return iterable<string, array{Example}>
     */
    public static function doctestProvider(): iterable
    {
        $config = static::configure();

        $fileScanner = new FileScanner($config);
        $sourceScanner = new SourceScanner();
        $extractor = new ExampleExtractor();

        foreach ($fileScanner->scan() as $filePath) {
            foreach ($sourceScanner->scanFile($filePath) as $target) {
                foreach ($extractor->extract($target) as $example) {
                    yield $example->getName() => [$example];
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Tests a docblock example.
     *
     * @param Example $example The example to test
     */
    #[Test]
    #[DataProvider('doctestProvider')]
    public function testDocblockExample(Example $example): void
    {
        $config = static::configure();

        if (self::$executor === null) {
            self::$executor = new ExampleExecutor($config->getBootstrap());
        }

        $result = self::$executor->execute($example);

        if (!$result->passed) {
            $this->fail($result->getErrorMessage());
        }

        $this->assertTrue(true);
    }
}

namespace Doctest\TestCase;

use Doctest\Executor\ExampleExecutor;
use Doctest\Parser\Example;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

/**
 * PHPUnit test case for a single doctest example.
 *
 * DoctestCase wraps an Example and executes it as a PHPUnit test.
 * It uses a shared ExampleExecutor instance for efficiency.
 *
 * @example Creating a test case
 *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
 *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Class_,
 *         filePath: __FILE__,
 *         docblock: 'docs',
 *         name: 'Test',
 *         line: 1,
 *     );
 *     $example = new \Doctest\Parser\Example('true', $target, 1, 0);
 *     $testCase = new \Doctest\TestCase\DoctestCase($example);
 *     $testCase->getName() // => 'Doctest: Test example #1 (line 1)'
 */
final class DoctestCase extends TestCase
{
    private static ?ExampleExecutor $executor = null;

    /**
     * @param Example $example The example to test
     * @param string|null $bootstrap Path to bootstrap file
     */
    public function __construct(
        private readonly Example $example,
        ?string $bootstrap = null,
    ) {
        $testName = $this->example->getTestName();
        assert($testName !== '');
        parent::__construct($testName);

        if (self::$executor === null) {
            self::$executor = new ExampleExecutor($bootstrap);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Returns the test name.
     *
     * @param bool $withDataSet Whether to include data set info (unused)
     */
    public function getName(bool $withDataSet = true): string
    {
        return $this->example->getTestName();
    }

    /**
     * Returns a string representation of the test.
     */
    public function toString(): string
    {
        return $this->example->getTestName();
    }

    /**

use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

 *

 * It uses a shared ExampleExecutor instance for efficiency.
 *
 * @example Creating a test case
 *     $target = new \Doctest\Scanner\Target(
 *         type: \Doctest\Scanner\TargetType::Class_,
 *         filePath: __FILE__,

 *     $testCase = new \Doctest\TestCase\DoctestCase($example);
 *     $testCase->getName() // => 'Doctest: Test example #1 (line 1)'
 */
final class DoctestCase extends TestCase
{
    private static ?ExampleExecutor $executor = null;

    /**
     * @param Example $example The example to test
     * @param string|null $bootstrap Path to bootstrap file
     */
    public function __construct(
        private readonly Example $example,
        ?string $bootstrap = null,
    ) {
        $testName = $this->example->getTestName();
        assert($testName !== '');
        parent::__construct($testName);

        if (self::$executor === null) {

    }

    public function toString(): string

         colors="true"

         executionOrder="depends,random"
         requireCoverageMetadata="true"
         beStrictAboutCoverageMetadata="true"
         beStrictAboutChangesToGlobalState="true"
         beStrictAboutOutputDuringTests="true"
         failOnAllIssues="true"
         failOnEmptyTestSuite="true"
         failOnRisky="true"
         failOnWarning="true"
         enforceTimeLimit="true"
         timeoutForSmallTests="1"
         timeoutForMediumTests="10"
         timeoutForLargeTests="60">
    <testsuites>
        <testsuite name="unit">
            <directory>tests/Unit</directory>
            <exclude>tests/Unit/PhpUnit/TestReporter/Legacy</exclude>
        </testsuite>
    </testsuites>
    <extensions>

            ignoreSuppressionOfErrors="true"
            ignoreSuppressionOfNotices="true"
            ignoreSuppressionOfPhpNotices="true"

            <directory>src</directory>

content.content:
# ScopeGuard Configuration

ScopeGuard configuration generated by the `/setup-toolkit-scope-guard` skill.

## Purpose

ScopeGuard is a first-party CLI that gives PHP the namespace visibility Rust spells `pub(crate)`,
`pub(super)`, and `pub(in path)`. PHP has two levels for anything a namespace exports — `public`,
which is public to the whole program, and nothing — so every helper a package needs internally is
reachable from everywhere, and the first caller outside the package that names it turns an
implementation detail into public API.

A declaration states its scope with a `@visibility` tag, and `scope-guard` reports every place the
sources name it from outside that scope.

```php
namespace App\Billing\Ledger;

/**
 * Appends entries to the ledger file.
 *
 * @visibility parent
 */
final class LedgerWriter
{
    public function append(Entry $entry): void { /* ... */ }
}
```

```
1. src/Http/InvoiceController.php:24 [out_of_scope]
   symbol: App\Billing\Ledger\LedgerWriter
   message: Class App\Billing\Ledger\LedgerWriter is not visible from namespace "App\Http": the
     declaration is marked "@visibility parent", so it may only be named from namespace "App\Billing"
     and its sub-namespaces. Move this instantiation into that namespace, or widen the declaration to
     "@visibility App".
```

The tag is ScopeGuard's own, not an extension of anyone else's vocabulary. It is checked by this
command, not by PHPStan: a static analyser's tag namespace belongs to that analyser, and a project
that adopts namespace visibility should not have to adopt a particular analyser with it.

## Command

Run:

```bash
vendor/bin/scope-guard --config=scope.yaml
```

Exit codes:

- `0`: no violations
- `1`: visibility violations found
- `2`: configuration or runtime error

## The `@visibility` Tag

A scope is one namespace plus everything below it, the way a Rust module contains its descendants.
The declaring namespace is always inside its own scope, so a declaration never hides from the code
next to it.

| Scope | Rust equivalent | Visible from |
|-------|-----------------|--------------|
| `public` | `pub` | Everywhere. Same as leaving the tag off; write it to state the intent. |
| `root` | `pub(crate)` | The outermost segment of the declaring namespace and everything below it. |
| `parent` | `pub(super)` | The namespace directly above the declaring one, and everything below it. |
| `namespace` | `pub(self)` | The declaring namespace and its sub-namespaces only. |
| `App\Billing` | `pub(in path)` | The named namespace and its sub-namespaces, plus the declaring namespace. |

For a grandparent and beyond, name the namespace: `@visibility App\Billing` says more about the
design than "two levels up" does, and it survives a move of the declaring class.

Several tags union. `@visibility namespace` plus `@visibility App\Console` opens the declaration to
its own namespace and to the console namespace, and to nothing else.

A namespace whose first segment is a single lowercase word collides with the keywords, so write it
with a leading backslash: `@visibility \legacy` names the namespace `legacy`, while
`@visibility legacy` is reported as a mistyped keyword.

Like every PHPDoc tag, `@visibility` only counts at the start of a comment line. Prose that names the
tag while explaining it is text, not a declaration.

### Where the tag can go

- Classes, interfaces, traits, and enums — restricts the whole type.
- Methods, properties, class constants, and enum cases — restricts one member of an otherwise public
  type. A member is never wider than its type: a `@visibility namespace` class keeps its untagged
  public methods inside that namespace too.

A scoped constructor is how a class stays publicly usable while only its own namespace may build it:

```php
final class Connection
{
    /**
     * @visibility namespace
     */
    public function __construct(private Socket $socket) {}
}
```

## What ScopeGuard Checks

ScopeGuard resolves names, not types. It parses each source file, applies the file's namespace and
its import table to every written name, and matches the result against the declarations it found.
That is the same question a module system asks — which paths may name this item — and it needs no
type inference to answer.

| Reference | Example |
|-----------|---------|
| instantiation | `new LedgerWriter()` |
| static call | `LedgerWriter::open()` |
| static property access | `LedgerWriter::$open` |
| constant access | `LedgerWriter::MODE`, `Suit::Hearts` |
| class name reference | `LedgerWriter::class` |
| instanceof check | `$value instanceof LedgerWriter` |
| inheritance | `extends`, `implements` |
| trait use | `use LedgerTrait;` |
| parameter, return, property type | `function write(LedgerWriter $writer): ?LedgerWriter` |
| catch type | `catch (LedgerFailure $failure)` |
| attribute | `#[LedgerMarker]` |

Member scopes are enforced wherever the member is reached through a named class, which covers
`X::method()`, `X::CONST`, `X::$prop`, and the constructor behind `new X()`. A member reached through
a variable — `$writer->append()` — is not resolved, because the type of `$writer` is not a name. The
class scope still holds there: the object had to be named somewhere to exist, and that name is
checked.

`self`, `static`, and `parent` are never reported. They can only name the class the reference is
already inside or one it inherits from, and that inheritance is checked where it is declared.

Member lookups follow declared parents, so a scope written on an inherited member answers for the
child class a reference names.

### Unusable tags

A scope that cannot be honoured is reported at the declaration under `invalid_scope`, because a tag
that silently resolves to nothing would drop the restriction it was written to add:

```
2. src/Billing/Ledger/LedgerWriter.php:8 [invalid_scope]
   symbol: App\Billing\Ledger\LedgerWriter
   message: Fix "@visibility parrent" on class App\Billing\Ledger\LedgerWriter: one bare lowercase
     word is read as a scope keyword, and "parrent" is not one of "public", "root", "parent",
     "namespace"; write the keyword you meant, or write "\parrent" to name the namespace.
```

The same applies to `@visibility parent` on a class in a root namespace (its parent is the global
namespace, which restricts nothing), to any scope keyword on a class in the global namespace, and to
`@visibility public` written next to a narrowing tag.

Because an unusable tag restricts nothing, one mistyped tag produces one violation at the
declaration instead of a violation at every reference.

## Configuration

Example `scope.yaml`:

```yaml
paths:
  - src

exclude:
  - 'src/Generated/*'

exempt_namespaces:
  - 'Tests'

report:
  reporter: ai
  order_by:
    - path
    - line
```

`paths` (default `['src']`) lists the files and directories to scan, relative to the config file
directory. Both declarations and references are read from these paths: a class outside them is
never checked, and code outside them is never reported.

`exclude` (default `[]`) is a list of fnmatch globs applied to project-relative paths. `*` crosses
`/` boundaries, so `src/Generated/*` removes a whole subtree.

`exempt_namespaces` (default `[]`) lists namespace prefixes whose code may name any declaration
regardless of its scope. A prefix exempts its whole subtree. Unusable tags are still reported inside
an exempt namespace — a tag that cannot be honoured is wrong wherever it is written.

Tests are the usual entry. PHP has no counterpart to Rust's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` declared inside
the module it covers, so a unit test of a namespace-scoped class necessarily sits in another
namespace. If the project scans its tests, exempt them:

```yaml
exempt_namespaces:
  - 'Tests'
```

## Reporter

`report.reporter` (default `ai`) selects the output format:

- `ai` — a structured report with per-violation remediation actions, intended for coding agents. The
  first line is `SCOPE_GUARD_PASSED` or `SCOPE_GUARD_FAILED`.
- `text` — concise human output.
- `json` — machine output for CI and other consumers.

`report.order_by` (default `['path', 'line']`) decides the order violations are printed in. Supported
fields are `path`, `line`, `rule`, and `symbol`. The order is decided by ScopeGuard rather than by
discovery order, so the same sources produce the same report on every platform and PHP version.

## How to Fix a Violation

### Move the reference into the scope

The usual answer: the code that wants the internal class belongs beside it.

### Give the namespace a public front door

When several namespaces want the same internal class, that is a missing entry point, not a missing
permission. Keep the internals scoped and export one public type from the owning namespace.

### Widen the declaration

If the scope was drawn too narrowly, widen it. Every message names the narrowest scope that would
admit the reference, so the fix does not have to be guessed.

Deleting the tag is not a fix. It removes the boundary instead of respecting it, which is the change
the tag exists to make visible.

## Relationship to DocGen

`doc-gen` reads the same tag. A scoped declaration carries a **Restricted visibility** notice on its
generated page, stating the scopes exactly as written, so the documentation says what is public API
and what is not. DocGen only reports the declaration; ScopeGuard is what enforces it.

## Prior Art

The tag has three ancestors, and borrows something from each:

- **phpDocumentor 1.x `@access private|protected|public`** — the original PHPDoc visibility tag,
  dropped once PHP gained real visibility keywords. It named the concept but could only repeat what
  the language already said.
- **PSR-19 `@internal`** — marks an element as internal to the project. It carries no scope, and
  nothing checks it.
- **Psalm `@psalm-internal Foo\Bar`** — restricts usage to a named namespace. This is the closest
  existing specification, and `@visibility Foo\Bar` means the same thing.

`@visibility` is a separate tag rather than a reuse of `@internal` because `@internal` accepts free
text (`@internal do not use`), which cannot be told apart from a scope. A dedicated tag keeps every
value meaningful, so a typo is a violation instead of a silently different scope.

## CI

`composer scope-guard` runs as a named step of the `lint` job on every supported
PHP minor, alongside formatting, PHPStan, PHPCompatibility, LocGuard, TreeGuard,
and Deptrac. See [GitHub Actions Configuration](github-actions.md).

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule;

use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\PhpDoc\PublicApiPhpDocErrorCollector;
use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\AnonymousClassDetector;
use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\ClassLikeKindLabel;
use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher;
use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use PHPStan\Rules\Rule;

/**
 * Requires PHPDoc comments on all public API elements.
 *
 * Checks classes, interfaces, traits, enums, their public methods
 * (including magic methods), public properties, and public constants.
 * Classes in restricted test namespaces are excluded entirely.
 *
 * @implements Rule<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike>
 */
final class RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule implements Rule
{
    /** @readonly */
    private AnonymousClassDetector $anonymousClassDetector;

    /** @readonly */
    private RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher $restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher;

    /** @readonly */
    private ClassLikeKindLabel $kindLabel;

    /** @readonly */
    private PublicApiPhpDocErrorCollector $errorCollector;

    /**
     * @param list<string> $restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes namespace prefixes to exclude from checks
     */
    public function __construct(
        array $restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes = ['Tests\\Unit', 'Tests\\Integration'],
        ?AnonymousClassDetector $anonymousClassDetector = null,
        ?RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher $restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher = null,
        ?ClassLikeKindLabel $kindLabel = null,
        ?PublicApiPhpDocErrorCollector $errorCollector = null,
    ) {
        $this->anonymousClassDetector = $anonymousClassDetector ?? new AnonymousClassDetector();
        $this->restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher = $restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher ?? new RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher($restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes);
        $this->kindLabel = $kindLabel ?? new ClassLikeKindLabel();
        $this->errorCollector = $errorCollector ?? new PublicApiPhpDocErrorCollector();
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike>
     */
    public function getNodeType(): string
    {
        return \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike::class;
    }

    /**
     * @param \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function processNode(\PhpParser\Node $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        if ($this->anonymousClassDetector->isAnonymous($node, $scope)) {
            return [];
        }

        if ($this->restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher->matches($node)) {
            return [];
        }

        $className = $node->name !== null ? $node->name->toString() : '';
        $kindLabel = $this->kindLabel->label($node);

        return $this->errorCollector->errors($node, $kindLabel, $className);
    }
}

use PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher;
use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use PHPStan\Rules\Rule;

/**
 * Requires PHPDoc comments on all public API elements.
 *
 * Checks classes, interfaces, traits, enums, their public methods
 * (including magic methods), public properties, and public constants.
 * Classes in restricted test namespaces are excluded entirely.
 *
 * @implements Rule<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike>
 */
final class RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule implements Rule
{
    /** @readonly */
    private AnonymousClassDetector $anonymousClassDetector;

    /** @readonly */
    private RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher $restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher;

    /** @readonly */
    private ClassLikeKindLabel $kindLabel;

    /** @readonly */
    private PublicApiPhpDocErrorCollector $errorCollector;

    /**
     * @param list<string> $restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes namespace prefixes to exclude from checks
     */
    public function __construct(
        array $restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes = ['Tests\\Unit', 'Tests\\Integration'],
        ?AnonymousClassDetector $anonymousClassDetector = null,
        ?RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher $restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher = null,
        ?ClassLikeKindLabel $kindLabel = null,
        ?PublicApiPhpDocErrorCollector $errorCollector = null,
    ) {
        $this->anonymousClassDetector = $anonymousClassDetector ?? new AnonymousClassDetector();
        $this->restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher = $restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher ?? new RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher($restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes);
        $this->kindLabel = $kindLabel ?? new ClassLikeKindLabel();
        $this->errorCollector = $errorCollector ?? new PublicApiPhpDocErrorCollector();
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike>
     */
    public function getNodeType(): string
    {
        return \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike::class;
    }

    /**
     * @param \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function processNode(\PhpParser\Node $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        if ($this->anonymousClassDetector->isAnonymous($node, $scope)) {
            return [];
        }

        if ($this->restrictedTestNamespaceMatcher->matches($node)) {
            return [];
        }

        $className = $node->name !== null ? $node->name->toString() : '';
        $kindLabel = $this->kindLabel->label($node);

        return $this->errorCollector->errors($node, $kindLabel, $className);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\ScopeGuard\Analysis\Declaration;

use function array_merge;

/**
 * Names the declaration keyword of a class-like and the types it builds on.
 *
 * @visibility parent
 */
final class ClassLikeKind
{
    /**
     * Returns the declaration keyword of a class-like.
     */
    public function label(\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node): string
    {
        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Interface_) {
            return 'interface';
        }

        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Trait_) {
            return 'trait';
        }

        return $node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Enum_ ? 'enum' : 'class';
    }

    /**
     * Returns the fully qualified parents, interfaces, and traits of a class-like.
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public function supertypes(\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node): array
    {
        $names = [];
        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Class_) {
            if ($node->extends !== null) {
                $names[] = $node->extends;
            }

            $names = array_merge($names, $node->implements);
        }

        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Interface_) {
            $names = array_merge($names, $node->extends);
        }

        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Enum_) {
            $names = array_merge($names, $node->implements);
        }

        foreach ($node->getTraitUses() as $traitUse) {
            $names = array_merge($names, $traitUse->traits);
        }

        $supertypes = [];
        foreach ($names as $name) {
            $supertypes[] = $name->toString();
        }

        return $supertypes;
    }
}

        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Trait_) {
            return 'trait';
        }

        return $node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Enum_ ? 'enum' : 'class';
    }

    /**
     * Returns the fully qualified parents, interfaces, and traits of a class-like.
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public function supertypes(\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node): array
    {
        $names = [];
        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Class_) {
            if ($node->extends !== null) {
                $names[] = $node->extends;
            }

            $names = array_merge($names, $node->implements);
        }

        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Interface_) {
            $names = array_merge($names, $node->extends);
        }

        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Enum_) {
            $names = array_merge($names, $node->implements);
        }

        foreach ($node->getTraitUses() as $traitUse) {
            $names = array_merge($names, $traitUse->traits);
        }

        $supertypes = [];
        foreach ($names as $name) {
            $supertypes[] = $name->toString();
        }

        return $supertypes;
    }

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\ScopeGuard\Analysis\Declaration;

use PhpAiToolkit\ScopeGuard\Analysis\Scope\NamespaceLineage;
use PhpAiToolkit\ScopeGuard\Analysis\Scope\VisibilityScopeResolver;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Collects the scoped declarations of one namespace group into the index.
 *
 * @visibility parent
 */
final class DeclarationCollector
{
    /** @readonly */
    private VisibilityScopeResolver $scopeResolver;

    /** @readonly */
    private NamespaceLineage $lineage;

    /** @readonly */
    private ClassLikeKind $classLikeKind;

    /**
     * Creates the collector from scope resolution, namespace ancestry, and kind naming.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?VisibilityScopeResolver $scopeResolver = null,
        ?NamespaceLineage $lineage = null,
        ?ClassLikeKind $classLikeKind = null,
    ) {
        $this->scopeResolver = $scopeResolver ?? new VisibilityScopeResolver();
        $this->lineage = $lineage ?? new NamespaceLineage();
        $this->classLikeKind = $classLikeKind ?? new ClassLikeKind();
    }

    /**
     * Records every class-like of the given nodes, with its members, in the index.
     *
     * @param list<\PhpParser\Node> $nodes
     */
    public function collect(array $nodes, string $path, DeclarationIndex $index): void
    {
        foreach ($nodes as $node) {
            if (!$node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike || !isset($node->namespacedName)) {
                continue;
            }

            $className = $node->namespacedName->toString();
            $namespace = $this->lineage->of($className);
            $index->addClass($className, $this->classLikeKind->supertypes($node), new Declaration(
                $className,
                $this->classLikeKind->label($node),
                $namespace,
                $this->scopeResolver->resolve($this->docComment($node), $namespace),
                $path,
                $node->getStartLine(),
            ));

            $this->collectMembers($node, $className, $namespace, $path, $index);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Records the scoped members of one class-like in the index.
     */
    public function collectMembers(
        \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node,
        string $className,
        string $namespace,
        string $path,
        DeclarationIndex $index,
    ): void {
        foreach ($node->getMethods() as $method) {
            $name = $method->name->toString();
            $this->addMember($index, $className, $name, sprintf('%s::%s()', $className, $name), 'method', $namespace, $path, $method);
        }

        foreach ($node->getProperties() as $property) {
            foreach ($property->props as $declaredProperty) {
                $name = $declaredProperty->name->toString();
                $this->addMember($index, $className, $name, sprintf('%s::$%s', $className, $name), 'property', $namespace, $path, $property);
            }
        }

        foreach ($node->getConstants() as $classConstant) {
            foreach ($classConstant->consts as $declaredConstant) {
                $name = $declaredConstant->name->toString();
                $this->addMember($index, $className, $name, sprintf('%s::%s', $className, $name), 'constant', $namespace, $path, $classConstant);
            }
        }

        foreach ($node->stmts as $statement) {
            if ($statement instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\EnumCase) {
                $name = $statement->name->toString();
                $this->addMember($index, $className, $name, sprintf('%s::%s', $className, $name), 'enum case', $namespace, $path, $statement);
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Records one member declaration read from its own PHPDoc comment.
     */
    public function addMember(
        DeclarationIndex $index,
        string $className,
        string $memberName,
        string $symbol,
        string $kind,
        string $namespace,
        string $path,
        \PhpParser\Node $node,
    ): void {
        $index->addMember($className, $memberName, new Declaration(
            $symbol,
            $kind,
            $namespace,
            $this->scopeResolver->resolve($this->docComment($node), $namespace),
            $path,
            $node->getStartLine(),
        ));
    }

    /**
     * Returns the raw PHPDoc text of a node, or null when it carries none.
     */
    public function docComment(\PhpParser\Node $node): ?string
    {
        $docComment = $node->getDocComment();

        return $docComment === null ? null : $docComment->getText();
    }
}

{
    public function testStoresExampleData(): void
    {
        $example = new DocExample('Adding numbers', '$sum // => 3', 'tag', 2);

        self::assertSame('Adding numbers', $example->description);
        self::assertSame('$sum // => 3', $example->code);
        self::assertSame('tag', $example->source);
        self::assertSame(2, $example->index);

    {

        self::assertNull($example->description);
        self::assertSame('render();', $example->code);
        self::assertSame('fence', $example->source);
        self::assertSame(0, $example->index);

content.content:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\TestClass;

use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;

/**
 * Validates that each public source method has a matching unit test method.
 */
final class PublicMethodTestCoverageValidator
{
    /** @readonly */
    private SourceUnitTestFileResolver $testFileResolver;

    /** @readonly */
    private TestMethodFileReader $testMethodFileReader;

    /** @readonly */
    private PublicMethodTestCoverageErrorBuilder $errorBuilder;

    /**
     * Creates a public method test coverage validator.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?SourceUnitTestFileResolver $testFileResolver = null,
        ?TestMethodFileReader $testMethodFileReader = null,
        ?PublicMethodTestCoverageErrorBuilder $errorBuilder = null,
    ) {
        $this->testFileResolver = $testFileResolver ?? new SourceUnitTestFileResolver();
        $this->testMethodFileReader = $testMethodFileReader ?? new TestMethodFileReader();
        $this->errorBuilder = $errorBuilder ?? new PublicMethodTestCoverageErrorBuilder();
    }

    /**
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function errors(\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassMethod $node, string $sourceFile): array
    {
        if (!$node->isPublic() || $node->isAbstract()) {
            return [];
        }

        $methodName = $node->name->toString();

        if (str_starts_with($methodName, '__')) {
            return [];
        }

        $testFile = $this->testFileResolver->resolve($sourceFile);
        if ($testFile === null || !is_file($testFile)) {
            return [];
        }

        $expectedPrefix = 'test' . ucfirst($methodName);
        foreach ($this->testMethodFileReader->methodNames($testFile) as $testMethod) {
            if (str_starts_with($testMethod, $expectedPrefix)) {
                return [];
            }
        }

        return [$this->errorBuilder->build($methodName, $expectedPrefix, $node->getStartLine())];
    }
}
